newsitem.title: USA: Wired IPO pricing on hold - Goldman.
newsitem.headline: Wired IPO pricing on hold - Goldman.

text.p: The initial public stock offering of Wired Ventures Inc., the publisher of Wired magazine, was not priced Thursday night as expected, according to the lead underwriter, Goldman Sachs.

No further information was immediately available, according to a spokeswoman at Goldman Sachs, who had been in contact with the firm's syndicate desk. But a further announcement might be pending, she said.
Earlier, a source close to one of the underwriters said the estimated price range had been slashed to $8 to $10 a share from the previous estimate of $12 to $14 each.

Sources familiar with the offering said the target number of shares to be sold had also been cut to 3 million from 4.75 million as the underwriters sought to price the issue. Goldman Sachs and co-underwriter Robertson Stephens had no immediate comment on the size of the offering.

Sources in the equity investment community warned that the deal was under threat and could possibly be pulled for a second time. In July, the deal was postponed amid a broad decline in high-technology and Internet stocks.
A number of investment professionals have called the bid overpriced, even at lower levels this time around.

The company also runs HotWired, a site on the Internet's World Wide Web geared for those who want to keep up with the latest digital developments. It also markets an Internet search engine called HotBot.
